input: Research local co-op grocery membership options

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Co-op options vary enormously by city and region — knowing the location determines which specific co-ops can actually be researched.
Whether this is for a single person, a couple, or a family changes which membership tiers are relevant and how to weigh cost-benefit.
The user may want a broad survey of all co-ops nearby, or a deep dive comparing a specific shortlist — this shapes how much ground to cover.
Co-op memberships often require an upfront equity buy-in (e.g. $100–$300) plus possible annual fees; a budget ceiling rules options in or out immediately.
What the user most wants from a co-op (lower prices, local/organic produce, community values, worker ownership, etc.) determines which criteria to prioritise in evaluation.
Knowing the intended output — a simple notes list, a comparison table, a recommendation — determines how the research should be structured and delivered.
The user may already have a strong lean toward a particular co-op model (consumer-owned vs. worker-owned) or may be completely open, which steers which details to emphasise.

gold.taskTitle: Research local co-op grocery membership options
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate co-op grocery stores in the user's area to determine whether joining one makes sense for them.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood are you searching in?
questions.description: Identifies the geographic area so only reachable co-ops are included in the research.

questions.title: Who will the membership cover — just you or a household?
questions.description: Determines whether individual or household/family membership tiers are most relevant to compare.

questions.title: How many co-ops do you want to research and compare?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user wants a broad landscape survey or a focused deep-dive on one or two options.

questions.title: Is there a maximum upfront or annual membership cost you have in mind?
questions.description: Sets a budget ceiling to immediately filter out co-ops whose buy-in or fees are out of range.

questions.title: What matters most to you in a co-op — price, values, produce quality, or something else?
questions.description: Establishes the primary evaluation criteria so the research highlights the most decision-relevant details.

questions.title: What format do you want the findings delivered in?
questions.description: Determines whether the output should be a quick summary, a side-by-side comparison table, a ranked recommendation, etc.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for consumer-owned versus worker-owned co-ops?
questions.description: Surfaces any existing lean toward a particular co-op model so the research can be steered accordingly.
